title: 3D culture and cryopreservation/thawing strategy of human induced pluripotent stem cells for spaceflight experiments.
study_design: Spaceflight-oriented 3D culture and cryopreservation/thawing method study.

experiments.model: Human iPSC 3D spheroids in a porous PDMS/VitroGel culture system
experiments.intervention: Integrated automated culture, cryoprotectant perfusion, −80°C freezing, storage, and thawing workflow
experiments.storage: −80°C freezer; duration not reported in abstract
experiments.result: The abstract reports cell survival exceeding 85% after thawing.
experiments.evidence_excerpt: achieving a cell survival rate exceeding 85% after thawing

main_finding: The abstract describes a 3D hiPSC culture and integrated cryopreservation workflow for spaceflight experiments with reported post-thaw survival above 85%.
limitations: Abstract-only; no unreported formulation, cooling rate, warming rate, storage duration, or replication details inferred.
Spaceflight module stability does not establish broader cryopreservation efficacy.
mechanism_claim: Protocol feasibility and survival are reported; no direct physical-ice or biological-pathway mechanism is established in the abstract.
reviewer: Luna extraction; root archived abstract review

title: Cryoaerosolization Enables Scalable Vitrification-Based Cell Cryopreservation
study_design: bioRxiv preprint testing continuous cryoaerosolization vitrification across cell types.

experiments.model: Human iPSCs and human dermal fibroblasts
experiments.intervention: Cryoaerosolization and rewarming of CPA-loaded micrometer-scale droplets
experiments.outcome_name: Post-thaw viability and hiPSC colony-forming capacity
experiments.result: The abstract reports greater than 90% post-thaw viability for hiPSCs and dermal fibroblasts, with retained colony-forming capacity additionally demonstrated in hiPSCs.

experiments.model: Human iPSCs, porcine red blood cells, and human dermal fibroblasts
experiments.intervention: Scalable cryoaerosolization vitrification using micrometer-scale droplets and liquid nitrogen
experiments.comparator: Conventional droplet vitrification described in the preprint
experiments.result: The abstract reports 94% recovery for red blood cells and processing throughput at least 100 mL/h.

main_finding: This preprint reports a high-throughput cryoaerosolization vitrification platform applied to hiPSCs, fibroblasts, and RBCs with high reported post-thaw outcomes.
limitations: Abstract-only extraction; no replication, storage duration, or detailed CPA composition inferred.
Cached abstract renders the CPA range as 190–25 wt%, while its significance statement says as little as 19 wt%; composition remains null pending primary-version verification.
Public indexed snippets contain body text, but complete primary text could not be archived; root direct request returned HTTP 429 and web opens 403, so no repeated retries were made.
Reported throughput and high viability do not establish closed-system sterility, multi-donor consistency, functional potency or long-duration cryostorage.
mechanism_claim: The abstract links performance to rapid droplet cooling/warming and vitrification; this is not independent proof of a specific biological protection pathway.
reviewer: Luna extraction; root archived abstract review
